significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish the form-(iii) relation that a "representational transition matches the true boundary condition" and that its presence and location predict the onset of confident extrapolation error across scientific laws and models. This would establish a behavioral phenomenon and a predictive internal correlate, fixing expectations for untested regime sweeps, although the "read-only" signal would not establish a causal mechanism for the errors; calibration work such as Ovadia et al., "Can You Trust Your Model's Uncertainty?" (NeurIPS 2019), underscores the practical value of predictors tied to failure onset rather than generic confidence alone. Verified-false and verified-true are distinguishable: failure of boundary-location and error-onset coupling would rule out encoded domain boundaries as this diagnostic, though it would not rule out scientific understanding encoded in another form. Under topic substitution, the generic topic would suggest probing whether scientific laws are represented, but not this boundary-to-error predictive coupling, so the score is supported by the claim-specific relation rather than the topic's importance.

reach.justification: The named handle is the "Domain-of-Validity Score (DVS)," combining boundary detectability, boundary-location accuracy, and error/boundary alignment into a "read-only diagnostic" that can audit a model before relying on its extrapolations, making it ex ante relative to deployment even though constructing the audit uses labeled regime sweeps. After per-model re-extraction, the conclusion predicts a transferable relation—higher-quality internal transitions should track the physical boundary and forecast error onset—rather than merely supplying a procedure for rediscovering an arbitrary direction. The asserted scope spans "chemistry, physics, biology, and materials" foundation models, with downstream use by researchers and practitioners who evaluate or gate scientific-model outputs, although the explicit concession that findings are "law- and model-specific" prevents treating DVS as a calibration-free universal threshold. Under topic substitution, the broad scientific-representation topic alone supplies neither DVS nor an advance warning of invalid extrapolation, so the reach comes from this claim-specific auditing handle.
